rule: The laws of motion hold identically in all inertial reference frames; in any such frame the laws of electrodynamics and mechanics take the same form, and the speed of light in vacuum is invariant, independent of the motion of source or observer. Force-free bodies move uniformly; a non-zero force produces an acceleration inversely proportional to the body's inertial mass.
result: A photon emitted at the base of a tower and absorbed at the top arrives with a measurably lower frequency than when emitted; equivalently, identical clocks placed at different heights in a stationary laboratory on Earth run at different rates, the higher clock running faster, with the fractional difference proportional to the gravitational potential difference between them.
gold_case: A uniform gravitational field is locally indistinguishable from a uniformly accelerated reference frame; equivalently, inertial mass equals gravitational (passive and active) mass exactly. The motion of a freely falling body is therefore independent of its composition, and physics in a small freely falling laboratory is that of special relativity.
gold_case_source: Einstein, A. (1907). Uber das Relativitatsprinzip und die aus demselben gezogenen Folgerungen. Jahrbuch der Radioaktivitat und Elektronik, 4, 411-462.
decoy_cases: Photons lose kinetic energy climbing out of a gravitational potential well via a Newtonian gravitational force acting on their relativistic mass E/c^2, and this energy loss appears as a frequency reduction (recombines Newtonian gravity with the photon energy-mass relation but does not yield a geometric theory of gravity and predicts no universal coupling to all clocks).

Time is an absolute universal parameter but electromagnetic oscillators are physically perturbed by proximity to mass through an unknown field coupling, so 'clocks' at different heights merely tick differently while true time is unchanged (rescues Newtonian absolute time at the cost of introducing a new ad hoc field that couples identically to every oscillator type ever tested).
abduction_notes: The gold case is not deducible from the Rule: special relativity plus Newtonian gravity predicts at most a partial effect and contains no principled reason why every species of clock (atomic, mechanical, biological, nuclear) must tick slower in the same way. It is not an induction from the Result either — a single observation of photon redshift in a tower licenses many possible patch theories (a Newtonian gravitational pull on photons, a dispersive vacuum, an ad hoc time-dilation field). The leap is to a structural identification between gravitation and non-inertial motion, which elevates a numerical coincidence (inertial mass equals gravitational mass, known since Newton and verified by Eotvos) to a defining principle of a new geometric theory. A language model that has read every modern physics text knows the finished product (general relativity) but the abductive task is to produce the principle *from* the Rule and Result without being cued by the name or the finished formalism; the temptation is to propose an energy-loss mechanism or an ad hoc time field rather than a universality principle.

rule: In samples of cellular nucleic acid extracted from any organism, the molar quantity of adenine equals that of thymine, and the molar quantity of guanine equals that of cytosine, while the ratio (A+T)/(G+C) varies between species. X-ray fibre diffraction of hydrated nucleic acid fibres shows a repeating helical structure with a 3.4 A axial spacing between stacked planar groups and a 34 A pitch, with strong meridional reflections consistent with a regular helix.
result: This nucleic acid is the physical carrier of heritable information in cells; it is stable across cell divisions, faithfully copied during replication, and its copying produces two daughter molecules each of which shares exactly one strand with the parent molecule, as shown by density-gradient isotope-labelling experiments.
gold_case: The molecule is a right-handed double helix of two antiparallel sugar-phosphate backbones whose inward-facing bases form specific hydrogen-bonded pairs (adenine with thymine, guanine with cytosine) stacked 3.4 A apart. Because each strand specifies the sequence of the other through this base-pairing rule, replication proceeds by strand separation and templated synthesis of a complementary partner, automatically producing two daughter duplexes each containing one parental strand.
gold_case_source: Watson, J. D. & Crick, F. H. C. (1953). Molecular structure of nucleic acids: A structure for deoxyribose nucleic acid. Nature, 171, 737-738.
decoy_cases: The molecule is a triple helix with the phosphate backbones on the inside and the bases projecting outward into the solvent; equimolarity of A/T and G/C reflects symmetric rotational positions of the three strands (fits some diffraction features but cannot generate a mechanism for sequence copying and puts hydrophilic phosphates in an energetically unfavourable interior).

The molecule is a single flexible strand that folds back on itself and forms hairpin loops whose paired regions happen to contain roughly equal amounts of A-T and G-C (explains Chargaff's ratios as a statistical consequence of folding but cannot explain species-specific variation in (A+T)/(G+C) nor semi-conservative replication).
abduction_notes: Chargaff's ratios on their own suggest a pairing but not a structure; the diffraction pattern on its own constrains symmetry but does not force complementarity; semi-conservative replication on its own constrains topology but not chemistry. The abductive step is to posit a single structural hypothesis — antiparallel, base-paired, right-handed duplex — that simultaneously explains every observation and, as a gift, *predicts* a copying mechanism that no element of the Rule or Result explicitly requires. A well-read LLM knows this answer as a retrieval fact; the test is whether, with the theory name and discoverers withheld, it produces the specific structural hypothesis rather than a plausible-but-wrong alternative such as Pauling's triple helix (published in 1953 by a Nobel laureate) or a folded single-strand hairpin model.

rule: Magnetic anomaly surveys of the ocean floor reveal a pattern of symmetric parallel stripes of normal and reversed remanent magnetisation running parallel to mid-ocean ridges, with the sequence of polarities mirrored on either side of the ridge axis and correlated with the independently dated chronology of geomagnetic reversals. Deep-ocean sediments thicken with distance from ridge axes, and ocean-floor basalts grow older monotonically with distance from ridges. The geometric outlines of continental shelves on opposite sides of the Atlantic fit together, and matching fossil floras and Precambrian basement rocks occur on now-separated continents.
result: Deep earthquakes occur along inclined planes that dip beneath island arcs and continental margins down to roughly 700 km, while shallow earthquakes cluster along mid-ocean ridges, transform faults, and those same arc systems. No ocean floor older than about 200 million years is found anywhere on Earth, although continental rocks are dated as old as about 4 billion years.
gold_case: Earth's outer shell consists of a small number of rigid lithospheric plates that move horizontally over a ductile asthenosphere. New oceanic lithosphere is created at mid-ocean ridges by upwelling and cooling magma, carrying its remanent magnetisation away symmetrically on both sides as a tape recorder of the reversing geomagnetic field; older oceanic lithosphere is consumed at convergent boundaries, descending into the mantle along inclined planes (subduction zones) where it generates the observed deep-earthquake distribution. Continents are passively rafted by the plates in which they are embedded.
gold_case_source: Hess, H. H. (1962). History of ocean basins, in Petrologic Studies; Vine, F. J. & Matthews, D. H. (1963) Nature 199, 947; Wilson, J. T. (1965) Nature 207, 343; Morgan, W. J. (1968) J. Geophys. Res. 73, 1959.
decoy_cases: The Earth has been expanding over geological time; new surface area is generated at ridges as the planet's radius grows, accounting for striping and the youth of ocean floors while keeping continents fixed to their underlying mantle (explains symmetric striping and ocean-floor youth but falsified by absence of expansion signal in paleomagnetic latitude data and by impossible energy budget).

Mid-ocean ridges are fixed loci of intense hydrothermal alteration that imprint striped remanent magnetisations reflecting successive reversals without any crustal motion; continental fit is coincidental or due to a former land bridge now subsided (explains the striping pattern without moving anything but cannot explain the age gradient away from ridges nor the subduction-zone earthquake geometry).
abduction_notes: Each observation individually permits local explanations: striping can be read as in situ reversal recording, continental fit as coincidence plus subsidence, deep earthquakes as local stress phenomena. The genuine abductive jump is to unify all of these under a single kinematic regime of moving rigid plates with creation at ridges and destruction at trenches — a hypothesis that was *rejected* as geologically implausible for half a century (continental drift, proposed in 1912, lacked a mechanism and was dismissed) and required combining data from marine geophysics, seismology, and palaeontology simultaneously. The model is not derivable from any one Rule component; it is a structural conjecture that retrospectively makes all of them obligatory. An LLM can recall the name 'plate tectonics' but the test is whether it proposes *this particular synthesis* when presented with the evidence shorn of its customary narrative framing, rather than defaulting to expanding-Earth or fixed-continent recombinations that were historically competitive.

rule: A diffusible small-molecule product of the mould Penicillium notatum inhibits the growth of gram-positive bacteria at concentrations that have no effect on mammalian cells in culture or in vivo. The compound acts only on bacteria that are actively dividing; bacteria held in stationary phase are unaffected and resume growth if the compound is washed out before division resumes.
result: Susceptible bacteria exposed to the compound during growth swell, become spherical or irregular, and ultimately burst (lyse), with leakage of cytoplasmic contents into the medium. Mammalian cells show no analogous effect at the same or far higher concentrations, and the compound does not inhibit bacterial protein, nucleic acid, or energy metabolism measured directly.
gold_case: Bacteria possess a rigid cell-wall layer of peptidoglycan whose final assembly step is the cross-linking of glycan strands by peptide bonds catalysed by transpeptidase enzymes. The compound is a structural analogue of the acyl-D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus of the peptidoglycan precursor and covalently inactivates these transpeptidases; during growth the bacterium therefore synthesises an incomplete cell wall, cannot resist internal osmotic pressure, and lyses. Mammalian cells have no peptidoglycan and no transpeptidase, so they are unaffected.
gold_case_source: Park, J. T. & Strominger, J. L. (1957). Mode of action of penicillin. Science, 125, 99-101. Tipper, D. J. & Strominger, J. L. (1965). PNAS, 54, 1133-1141.
decoy_cases: The compound is selectively concentrated inside bacterial cells by a transport system absent in mammals and there inhibits a universal cellular process (protein synthesis or DNA replication); growth dependence reflects the fact that non-growing bacteria do not require the inhibited process (explains mammalian-sparing but contradicts the Rule's direct observation that protein, nucleic acid, and energy metabolism are not inhibited).

The compound disrupts the bacterial plasma membrane by intercalation, and only growing cells are lysed because membrane turnover at division sites exposes new intercalation targets; mammalian membranes differ in lipid composition and resist intercalation (accounts for lysis and selectivity but does not explain why the compound is a small acyl-peptide analogue nor why it covalently labels specific proteins).
abduction_notes: The Result has a straightforward restatement — 'the compound kills growing bacteria and not mammalian cells' — and many mechanisms can bridge that gap (selective uptake, membrane disruption, ribosomal specificity). The abductive leap is to posit a bacterium-specific *structural target* — peptidoglycan cross-linking — whose existence in 1928 was itself only partially established, and to identify the compound as a *substrate analogue* of a specific enzymatic step. This hypothesis is parsimonious precisely because it simultaneously explains mammalian sparing (no analogous structure), the growth requirement (transpeptidase acts only during wall synthesis), lysis (osmotic rupture follows from a weakened wall), and the absence of effects on central metabolism. A language model has encyclopedic knowledge of beta-lactam mechanism but the test is whether, shown only the phenomenology, it proposes substrate-analogue inhibition of cell-wall cross-linking rather than the more obvious guesses of selective uptake or membrane damage that dominated the early literature.

rule: Organisms of every species produce many more offspring than can survive to reproduce, so mortality before reproduction is high and selective. Individual organisms within a species vary in their morphological, physiological, and behavioural traits, and many such traits are heritable from parent to offspring with fidelity greater than chance. The environments inhabited by different populations of a species differ in their physical, biotic, and resource characteristics.
result: Geographically isolated populations of the same ancestral species come, over many generations, to differ systematically in traits in ways that correspond to the distinctive features of their environments (beak shape to available seeds, coat colour to background, metabolism to thermal regime). Over longer timescales, lineages diversify into groups of related species exhibiting graded similarities and fitting a nested hierarchical classification, and the fossil record shows a similar pattern of progressive modification and divergence.
gold_case: Heritable variants that confer, in a given environment, even a small increase in the expected number of surviving fertile offspring their bearers produce (relative to alternative variants) will rise in frequency in successive generations, purely as a consequence of differential reproduction. Accumulated and compounded over many generations, this differential reproduction of heritable variants produces adaptation of populations to their environments and, given reproductive isolation, the branching divergence of lineages into new species — a process of descent with modification with no external directing agent.
gold_case_source: Darwin, C. & Wallace, A. R. (1858). On the tendency of species to form varieties; and on the perpetuation of varieties and species by natural means of selection. J. Proc. Linn. Soc. London. Zool. 3, 45-62. Darwin, C. (1859). On the Origin of Species. London: John Murray.
decoy_cases: Organisms alter their bodies and behaviours during their lifetimes in response to environmental demands (use and disuse), and these acquired modifications are transmitted to offspring; adaptation is therefore the accumulation of such inherited acquired characters over generations (explains adaptation but contradicts the Rule's stipulation that only heritable variation is transmitted, and is refuted by modern molecular genetics of inheritance).

Environmental stress directly induces the specific adaptive variants that are required in germline cells; mutation is therefore directed, not random, and variation is generated on demand in response to selective pressures (explains apparent goal-directedness of adaptation but is not required by any element of the Rule, which specifies only pre-existing heritable variation, and is inconsistent with the Luria-Delbruck fluctuation test).
abduction_notes: The three components of the Rule — overproduction, heritable variation, environmental differentiation — together make the gold case look almost deductive in retrospect, which is precisely why the historical abductive step was so hard: for two millennia prior, the observation of adaptation had been taken as prima facie evidence of design or internal teleology. The creative leap is to see that a non-teleological statistical mechanism — merely that the most-reproduced variants become more common — is *sufficient* to generate every feature of the Result, including apparent purposiveness. An LLM recites natural selection fluently; the test is whether, given only the ingredients, it generates *this* mechanism rather than a Lamarckian acquired-character account or a directed-mutation account, both of which are historically plausible and both of which dominated much of the 19th-century literature.

rule: A set A is said to have at least as many elements as a set B when there exists an injection from B into A; A and B have the same cardinality when there exists a bijection between them. The natural numbers, the integers, and the rational numbers can all be placed in bijection with one another, and any set that can be placed in bijection with the natural numbers is called countable. Every real number in the interval [0,1] has a decimal expansion as an infinite sequence of digits drawn from {0,1,...,9}.
result: No explicit enumeration r_1, r_2, r_3, ... of real numbers in [0,1] ever produced has succeeded in containing every real number in that interval; for every proposed enumeration one can exhibit a real number demonstrably absent from the list. Yet the rationals in [0,1], which are dense in that interval, *are* enumerable by familiar diagonal-fraction listings.
gold_case: Given any purported enumeration r_1, r_2, ... of reals in [0,1], construct a new real r* whose n-th decimal digit differs from the n-th decimal digit of r_n (say by adding 1 mod 10, avoiding the 0.999... = 1.000... ambiguity). Then r* is in [0,1] but differs from every r_n in at least one digit, so r* is not in the enumeration. Therefore no enumeration of the reals exists, and the set of reals is strictly larger in cardinality than the set of naturals; infinities come in different sizes, and the power set operation strictly increases cardinality.
gold_case_source: Cantor, G. (1891). Uber eine elementare Frage der Mannigfaltigkeitslehre. Jahresbericht der Deutschen Mathematiker-Vereinigung, 1, 75-78.
decoy_cases: The enumeration fails only because human beings cannot complete an infinite listing in finite time; in principle, given an infinite time, one could list the reals exactly as one lists the rationals (conflates epistemic and ontic limits; the proof is not about practical listability but about logical impossibility).

There are only countably many 'definable' real numbers (those specifiable by a finite description in some fixed formal language); the rest do not really exist as individual objects but only as a collective, so claims about their cardinality are meaningless (a constructivist retreat that avoids rather than answers the cardinality question, and inconsistent with classical set theory's use of these objects).
abduction_notes: The Rule gives the definition of cardinality and the fact that many 'larger-looking' sets (integers, rationals) are actually the same size as the naturals — priming the intuition that *all* infinite sets might be the same size. The Result reports only a recurring failure, never a proof of impossibility. The abductive leap is twofold: first, to conjecture that the failure is not contingent but necessary, and second, to *construct a specific counterexample by diagonalisation* that converts a supposed enumeration into its own contradiction. This technique — self-referential construction of an object that escapes every row of a list by disagreeing with the row's own diagonal entry — had no prior exemplar in mathematics and spawned an entire pattern of argument (Russell's paradox, Godel's incompleteness, Turing's halting problem, Tarski's undefinability). An LLM 'knows' the diagonal argument; the test is whether, given only the Rule and Result, it produces *the diagonal construction* rather than, say, a topological density argument or a retreat into constructivism.

rule: The compound with molecular formula C6H6 is unusually stable: it is a liquid at room temperature, resistant to the addition reactions (hydrogenation, halogenation without catalyst, hydration) that rapidly consume typical unsaturated hydrocarbons, yet it readily undergoes substitution in which one hydrogen is replaced by another group. Monosubstituted derivatives C6H5X occur in only one isomeric form for every X tested. Disubstituted derivatives C6H4X2 or C6H4XY occur in exactly three isomeric forms per substituent combination, regardless of substituent identity.
result: Every carbon atom in the molecule is chemically equivalent to every other (from the uniqueness of the monosubstituted product); chemical substitution at any of the six positions is energetically similar; and a kinetic study of hydrogenation yields an enthalpy of hydrogenation substantially less negative per unsaturation than that of a comparable open-chain triene. Nuclear magnetic resonance studies show that all six protons are magnetically equivalent and that a strong ring current is induced when the molecule is placed in a magnetic field.
gold_case: The six carbon atoms form a planar, regular closed hexagonal ring; each carbon is sp2-hybridised and contributes one p-electron to a set of pi-molecular orbitals delocalised over the entire ring. This cyclic delocalisation of six pi-electrons (obeying what later became the 4n+2 rule for aromaticity) accounts simultaneously for the equivalence of all positions, the three-isomer rule for disubstitution, the enhanced thermodynamic stability relative to an acyclic triene (resonance energy), the single NMR proton signal, and the diatropic ring current.
gold_case_source: Kekule, A. (1865). Sur la constitution des substances aromatiques. Bulletin de la Societe Chimique de Paris, 3, 98-110. (Later refined by Huckel molecular orbital theory, 1931.)
decoy_cases: The molecule is a bicyclic prismane (two stacked triangles joined by three bonds); the six carbons are equivalent by the threefold symmetry, and substitution resistance follows from ring strain (predicts wrong isomer counts for disubstitution and is dramatically strained, not stable).

The molecule is an open-chain conjugated hexatriene whose pi-conjugation is stabilised by end-to-end electronic delocalisation; carbon equivalence arises from rapid bond-shift tautomerism (predicts three kinds of carbon, not one, and cannot account for the three-isomer rule or the ring current).
abduction_notes: Substitution patterns heavily constrain the connectivity: any hypothesis with non-equivalent carbons is excluded by the single monosubstitution product, and any hypothesis with the wrong number of symmetry-equivalent pairs is excluded by the three-isomer rule. The historical abductive leap was to propose a *cyclic* structure with alternating double bonds at a time when cyclic organic molecules were not part of the received structural vocabulary, and then the second leap — delocalisation — to explain why the resulting molecule is so much less reactive than a linear triene of equal unsaturation. An LLM will recite 'benzene' immediately on hearing C6H6; the discipline of the task is to force it to produce the *structural argument* from the phenomenology without name-cueing, and then to propose delocalisation (rather than, say, rapid classical bond tautomerism, Kekule's original interpretation) to account for the stability and NMR observations.

rule: Two countries, call them Alpha and Beta, each possess a fixed stock of labour which is the sole factor of production and is mobile between industries within a country but not between countries. Each country can produce two goods, wine and cloth, and for each good a country has some per-unit labour requirement (hours per unit) that is technologically fixed. Consumers in each country want both goods. International exchange occurs only through voluntary bilateral trade at a common terms-of-trade price ratio. Country Alpha has strictly lower per-unit labour requirements for both wine and cloth than country Beta.
result: When the two countries move from autarky to trade at a suitably chosen terms of trade, the total world output of both wine and cloth can increase simultaneously, and the consumption possibilities of *both* Alpha and Beta expand beyond their autarky levels — including Beta, the country that is absolutely less efficient at producing either good.
gold_case: The gains from trade depend on differences in *relative* (opportunity) costs across countries, not on absolute productivity levels. Even if Alpha can produce every good with less labour per unit than Beta, the ratios of labour requirements between the two goods generally differ across the countries. Each country should specialise in the good whose *opportunity cost* (units of the other good foregone per unit produced) is lower for it than for its partner, and trade for the other good at any terms of trade lying strictly between the two countries' autarky opportunity-cost ratios. Both countries then enjoy consumption bundles outside their autarky production frontiers.
gold_case_source: Ricardo, D. (1817). On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation. London: John Murray. Chapter 7 ('On Foreign Trade').
decoy_cases: Gains from trade arise because the less efficient country can pay its workers lower wages; trade therefore benefits both partners only when the wage differential offsets the productivity gap, otherwise the more efficient country captures all surplus (confuses absolute with relative cost and erroneously predicts that no trade is beneficial to the more efficient partner when wages equilibrate).

Because Alpha is absolutely more efficient in both industries, trade is a zero- or negative-sum game for Alpha; the observed mutual gains therefore arise from non-economic factors such as taste differences, risk-sharing, or access to otherwise unavailable varieties (denies the purely productive basis of gains from trade and cannot account for the classic simple model in which tastes are identical).
abduction_notes: Absolute-advantage intuitions are the default: a layperson, told Alpha is strictly more productive, infers Alpha has nothing to gain from trade. The Rule as stated invites this conclusion. The abductive leap is to see that the *relevant* comparison is not absolute labour productivity but the *ratio* of labour productivities within each country — the opportunity cost — which can differ across countries even when one country is absolutely more productive in every good. This is counter-intuitive enough that it has been called the only non-trivial and non-obvious proposition in the social sciences. An LLM can define comparative advantage on demand; the test is whether, given the stipulation that Alpha is absolutely more productive *in both goods*, it still proposes the relative-cost mechanism rather than retreating into wage-differential or taste-heterogeneity recombinations.

rule: Gravitational dynamics at scales from the solar system to galaxy clusters is well described by a geometric theory of gravity whose weak-field slow-motion limit reduces to an inverse-square force law sourced by all forms of mass-energy. The distribution of luminous matter in galaxies and clusters (stars, gas, dust) can be directly measured with high precision across the electromagnetic spectrum.
result: Rotation curves of spiral galaxies, measured in HI and optical tracers, remain flat out to radii far beyond the edge of the luminous disk, rather than falling as r^{-1/2} as would be expected if all gravitating mass were in the luminous component. Galaxy clusters show velocity dispersions, gravitational lensing signals, and hot-gas hydrostatic-equilibrium temperatures implying total masses roughly five to ten times the summed masses of all luminous components. The acoustic peak structure of the cosmic microwave background is fit by a cosmological model only when non-baryonic pressure-less matter contributes roughly five times more mass-energy density than baryonic matter, a conclusion independently supported by the primordial abundance of light elements.
gold_case: A non-luminous, non-baryonic form of matter, dominant by a factor of roughly five over ordinary baryonic matter, pervades galaxies, clusters, and the universe at large. It interacts gravitationally (hence its dynamical effects) but its electromagnetic couplings are negligible (hence invisibility), and it behaves as a cold, nearly pressure-less fluid on cosmological scales, permitting the growth of structure and matching the CMB acoustic peak ratios and the primordial light-element abundances simultaneously.
gold_case_source: Zwicky, F. (1933). Die Rotverschiebung von extragalaktischen Nebeln. Helvetica Physica Acta, 6, 110-127. Rubin, V. C. & Ford, W. K. (1970). Astrophys. J., 159, 379. Peebles, P. J. E. (1982). Astrophys. J. Lett., 263, L1.
decoy_cases: The law of gravity itself is modified at low accelerations (below roughly 1.2e-10 m/s^2), with gravitational acceleration transitioning smoothly from the Newtonian regime to a deep-MOND regime where the effective acceleration scales as the square root of the Newtonian value; flat rotation curves follow automatically and no dark matter is required (accounts elegantly for galactic rotation curves but fails at cluster scales — residual mass discrepancies remain after applying MOND — and cannot reproduce the CMB acoustic peaks without introducing additional dark matter anyway).

The missing gravitating mass is composed of dim baryonic objects — brown dwarfs, old cool white dwarfs, or primordial black holes of stellar mass — distributed in galactic halos and detectable only through gravitational microlensing (contradicted by microlensing null results on solar-mass compact objects, by the primordial deuterium abundance constraining baryonic density, and by the CMB acoustic peaks).
abduction_notes: The Result admits several prima facie explanations: modify gravity, postulate hidden baryons, or postulate a new form of matter. The abductive task is to identify the *unique* hypothesis that simultaneously fits every component of the Result — flat rotation curves, cluster dynamics, gravitational lensing, CMB acoustic peaks, primordial nucleosynthesis — under a common set of parameters. Cold non-baryonic dark matter is that hypothesis; the alternatives each succeed on a subset and fail on another. The abductive virtue is structural: a single novel substance with a small number of properties (gravitational coupling, negligible electromagnetic coupling, cold, non-baryonic) is sufficient to explain observations at seven orders of magnitude in length and at completely different epochs of cosmic history. An LLM 'knows' dark matter; the test is whether, given the ingredients, it proposes a single-agent explanation rather than a patchwork of separate causes for each phenomenon.

rule: In nineteenth-century European maternity hospitals, the mortality rate among women admitted for childbirth to wards staffed by physicians was routinely three to five times the mortality rate in wards staffed by midwives within the same institution. Physicians in the era routinely performed morning anatomical dissections of cadavers from the previous day's deaths and then, without changing clothes or washing hands, proceeded directly to examine women in labour; midwives performed no such dissections. A prominent obstetrician died after cutting his hand during an autopsy, and his terminal illness was clinically indistinguishable from the puerperal (childbed) fever that killed the women in his ward.
result: When a hand-washing intervention in a solution of chlorinated lime (which neutralised the characteristic cadaveric odour) was instituted between autopsy work and ward examinations, maternal mortality on the physicians' ward dropped from approximately 10% to approximately 1%, converging with the mortality rate on the midwives' ward. No pharmacological treatment, change in admissions, change in diet, or change in ventilation was made.
gold_case: Certain diseases — specifically including puerperal fever and the physician's fatal illness after the autopsy cut — are caused by a specific transmissible microbial agent that can be physically carried from one host (including a cadaver) to another on the hands or instruments of intermediaries; interrupting this physical transmission chain by antiseptic handwashing prevents the disease, and different microbial species cause different specific diseases. This constitutes a germ theory of contagious disease.
gold_case_source: Semmelweis, I. (1861). Die Atiologie, der Begriff und die Prophylaxis des Kindbettfiebers. Pest, Vienna, Leipzig. Pasteur, L. (1878). Mem. Acad. Sci., 23. Koch, R. (1876). Beitrage zur Biologie der Pflanzen, 2, 277-310.
decoy_cases: An unidentified chemical poison ('cadaveric particles' or 'decaying animal matter') present on physicians' hands is absorbed into the bloodstream of parturient women via genital-tract lesions, causing toxic systemic illness; chlorinated lime neutralises the poison chemically (Semmelweis's own early non-microbial formulation: explains hand-wash efficacy but not the living, self-reproducing character of the infectious agent and cannot explain how the same disease is transmitted between living patients without autopsy contact).

A miasmatic exhalation from autopsy rooms and from diseased patients saturates the clothing and air around physicians and is conveyed to new patients; chlorinated lime works because it eliminates the characteristic cadaveric odour that marks the miasma (accounts for some observations but contradicts the efficacy of handwashing alone with unchanged clothing and air, and makes no prediction of a specific replicating agent).
abduction_notes: The hand-washing intervention establishes that physical transfer of *something* on hands causes disease; it does not by itself establish what that something is. The historical non-microbial options were vigorous: cadaveric chemical poison (Semmelweis's original hypothesis), miasma (the orthodoxy of the day), contagium (a physical but unspecified principle). The abductive leap is to identify the agent as a *living, self-reproducing organism* specific to each disease — this requires unifying evidence from obstetric wards, surgery (Lister), fermentation (Pasteur), and anthrax and tuberculosis (Koch), none of which is implied by any single observation. An LLM knows germ theory as a received idea; the test is whether, given the obstetric evidence alone and no priming, it generates the specifically *microbial and species-specific* hypothesis rather than settling for the chemical-poison or miasmatic account that each individually explain the hand-wash effect.
